title: Why the order of matrix multiplication matters
examples: Why is AB not equal to BA for matrices?
What does multiplying two matrices mean?
Does order matter in matrix multiplication?

explain.say: Do you put on your socks then your shoes, or your shoes then your socks? Order matters! Matrices are the same. Multiplying two matrices means doing one move, then the other. Look at the left side.

draw.text: Why the order of matrix multiplication matters

explain.say: Left side: start with the point 1, 0. Turn it a quarter turn anticlockwise and it lands at 0, 1. Then flip it in the x-axis, and it lands at 0, minus 1. Can you picture it pointing down?
Now the right side: same two moves, other order. Flip 1, 0 in the x-axis first. It sits on the axis, so it stays at 1, 0. Then turn it a quarter turn: it lands at 0, 1, pointing up.
Down on the left, up on the right! The same two moves in a different order give different answers. So for matrices, A times B is usually not B times A. And remember, A B means do B first, then A.
Well done! Ordinary numbers do not care about order, but matrices do. Animators and robot builders must get the order right, or a robot arm turns its hand before moving its elbow.

faq.q: Why is AB not equal to BA for matrices?
faq.a: Each matrix is a move, and AB means do B first, then A. Doing two moves in a different order can end in a different place, so AB and BA are usually different.

faq.q: What does multiplying two matrices mean?
faq.a: It means joining two transformations into one. The product matrix does the first move and then the second in a single step.

faq.q: Does order matter in matrix multiplication?
faq.a: Yes, almost always. Only some special pairs, like two rotations about the same point, give the same result in either order.

faq.q: In AB, which matrix acts first?
faq.a: B acts first, then A, because the product acts on a point written on the right: A times B times the point.

faq.q: How do you multiply two 2 by 2 matrices?
faq.a: Each entry is a row of the first matrix times a column of the second: multiply matching numbers and add.
asks: What is the rule for matrix multiplication?

facts: Matrix multiplication is not commutative: in general AB ≠ BA.
In the product AB applied to a vector, the transformation B is applied first, then A.

quiz.say: In the product AB acting on a point, which transformation happens first?
quiz.show: In the product AB acting on a point, which transformation happens first?
quiz.why: AB times the point means B acts on the point, then A acts on the result.

wrong.0: A acts second, because B is closer to the point.
wrong.2: They happen one after another, combined into one matrix.

quiz.say: Which statement is true for most pairs of matrices?
quiz.show: Which statement is true for most pairs of matrices?

wrong.0: Only special pairs give the same result in either order.
wrong.1: A product of two matrices is zero only in special cases.
